## Learning objectives

- Manipulate data with the dplyr package
- Join two datasets (tables) using a common key
- Spot issues in real datasets (outliers, missing values) and handle them

---

## Recap

Over the past three weeks we've looked at R basics, data structures, importing and basic visualisation. This week focuses on data transformation using the tidyverse, mainly dplyr.

---

## Data transformation with dplyr

dplyr gives concise verbs for common tasks:

- filter() — pick rows
- arrange() — reorder rows
- select() — pick columns
- mutate() — create/transform columns
- summarise() — collapse to summaries

We'll use the built-in mpg dataset for examples.

---

### Inspect mpg

```{webr}
#| warning: false
#| autorun: true
library(tidyverse)
str(mpg)
```

---

### filter() — pick observations

Select Audi cars? Engine displacement > 2?

```{webr}
#| warning: false
#| autorun: true
filter(mpg, manufacturer=="audi")
filter(mpg, displ > 2)
```

---

### filter() - multiple conditions

Combine conditions with `&` and `|`, or use `%in%` for membership.

```{webr}
#| warning: false
#| autorun: true
filter(mpg, displ > 2 & cyl > 6)
filter(mpg, manufacturer=="audi", year==1999)
filter(mpg, manufacturer=="audi" & year==1999)
```

---

<!-- ### Sampling and pipes

Use `sample_frac` or `sample_n` to take random samples. Use `%>%` to chain operations.

```{webr}
#| warning: false
#| autorun: true
sample_frac(mpg, 0.05, replace=TRUE)
sample_n(mpg, 10, replace=TRUE)
```

--- -->

### arrange() — reordering rows

```{webr}
#| warning: false
#| autorun: true
rio2016Medals <- read_csv("Rio2016.csv")
arrange(rio2016Medals, Country)
```

---

### arrange() — Descending and multi-column ordering:

```{webr}
#| warning: false
#| autorun: true
arrange(rio2016Medals, desc(Country))
arrange(rio2016Medals, desc(Gold), desc(Silver), desc(Bronze))
```

---

### select() — selecting columns

```{webr}
#| warning: false
#| autorun: true
select(mpg, manufacturer, hwy)
select(mpg, starts_with("d"))
```

---

### Combine select + filter + arrange with pipes:

```{webr}
#| warning: false
#| autorun: true
mpg %>% 
  select(manufacturer, hwy) %>% 
  filter(manufacturer != "chevrolet" & hwy >=20) %>%
  arrange(desc(manufacturer))
```

---

### mutate() — new variables

Create a Total column in the medals data?
Mutate only affects later steps in the pipe unless you assign it to a variable.

```{webr}
#| warning: false
#| autorun: true
mutate(rio2016Medals, Total = Gold + Silver + Bronze)
```

---

### summarise() and group_by()

```{webr}
#| warning: false
#| autorun: true
summarise(mpg, avg = mean(hwy))
group_by(mpg, year, manufacturer) %>% summarise(count = n())
group_by(mpg, manufacturer) %>% summarise(count = n())
```

---

## Combining datasets (joins)

Use the nycflights13 package to demonstrate joins between relational tables.

```{webr}
#| warning: false
#| autorun: true
library(tidyverse)
library(nycflights13)

nycflights13::airlines
nycflights13::airports
```

---

### Combining datasets (left join)

Add full airline name to flights:

```{webr}
#| warning: false
#| autorun: true
flights2 <- flights %>% select(year:day, hour, origin, dest, tailnum, carrier)
flights2 %>% left_join(airlines, by = "carrier")
```

---

## Working with real data — Free School Meals (FSM)

```{webr}
#| warning: false
#| autorun: true
meals <- read_csv("freeschoolmeals.csv")
head(meals)
```

---

### FSM - Common issues

- sentinel outlier value: 9999 (represents suppressed values < 5)
- NA values for missing data

Check summary and mean behaviour:

```{webr}
#| warning: false
#| autorun: true
summary(meals$FSMTaken)
mean(meals$FSMTaken)
mean(meals$FSMTaken, na.rm=TRUE)
```

---

### FSM - Filter out 9999 and handle NA

```{webr}
#| warning: false
#| autorun: true
actualFSMTaken <- meals$FSMTaken[meals$FSMTaken != 9999]
length(actualFSMTaken)
mean(actualFSMTaken, na.rm = TRUE)
```

Or use dplyr to keep NA and exclude 9999:

```{webr}
#| warning: false
#| autorun: true
filter(meals, (FSMTaken < 9999 | is.na(FSMTaken))) %>% count()
filter(meals, (FSMTaken < 9999 | is.na(FSMTaken))) %>% 
  mutate(newFSMTaken = ifelse(is.na(FSMTaken), floor(mean(FSMTaken, na.rm = TRUE)), FSMTaken))
```

---

### Missing values — simple imputation example

```{webr}
#| warning: false
#| autorun: true
y <- c(4,5,6,NA)
is.na(y)
y[is.na(y)] <- mean(y, na.rm = TRUE)
y
```

## Important points (highlight)

- Always inspect your data: summary(), str(), View()
- Watch out for sentinel values (e.g. 9999) and decide how to treat them before computing summaries
- Missing values (NA) must be handled explicitly (na.rm or imputation)
- dplyr verbs (filter, select, arrange, mutate, summarise) + pipes make transformation readable and reproducible
- Use joins carefully: pick the right join (left/inner/full) and check for unexpected NAs after the join
- When sampling or random processes, set a seed to make results reproducible
